title: Sweep across a Boolean word
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a Boolean selector encoding, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any optional state $oq$, output register $r$, Boolean tag $b$, auxiliary tape content $\tau_C$, integer position $z_C$, Boolean word $rest$, and natural numbers $i,j$, running the constructed machine for $j$ steps from its waiting-decision configuration with output tape content consisting of $i$ true bits, then $j$ false bits, then $rest$, and auxiliary head at $i$, yields the same waiting-decision configuration with the first $i+j$ bits true, followed by $rest$, and auxiliary head at $i+j$.
